propositions: A model class configured with provider=bedrock and a canonical versioned Bedrock id containing a colon has its configured provider silently discarded because _resolve_target treats any colon as already-provider-qualified.

The dropped provider causes infer_provider to read a fragment of the model id (e.g. 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1') as the provider, which the factory rejects, degrading the review gate to INDETERMINATE with a misleading 'unknown provider' error that names part of the model id.
The qualified/unqualified decision is unified into one shared helper split_provider_qualifier used by both _resolve_target and infer_provider so the two deciders cannot drift apart.

An explicitly configured provider must be checked first before scanning the model string, otherwise inputs like _resolve_target('openai:gpt-4o', provider='bedrock') still silently drop the configured provider.
A conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pair raises LLMConfigError rather than silently picking a winner, while bare unqualified ids continue to infer byte-for-byte as before.
The qualified/unqualified decision should be made against the registered provider set to catch typo'd providers with a proper diagnostic, delegated to child ticket 7b22 which keeps this ticket open.
